analysis.title: GS Kaplan - GS Global Equities Call 6 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities are bid again: SPX futures +25bps, NDX +40bps, RTY +5bps. Bond yields eased (UST10yr -3bps at 5.27%, UST30yr -3bps at 5.63%, France 10yr -11bps at 4.74%, Italy 10yr -11bps at 4.5%, German 10yr -3bps at 3.46%) and WTI fell 2.2% to $87.45.

France's Marine Le Pen, currently leading polls ahead of next year's election, proposed a sharp deficit reduction, which helped European sentiment. Bessent said the US can 'very quickly' bend the US debt curve.
Middle East: reports say Yemen recaptured critical territory from the Houthis near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and Saudi Arabia confirmed its East-West pipeline is flowing at 5.8mbd.

GS US Economics Analyst: higher rates hit residential investment hardest. Mortgage rates are up more than 1pp since February and most borrowers hold mortgages priced well below market rates, which cuts the incentive to move. GS expects a drag of about 2pp on annualized residential investment growth in 2026Q4 and 1pp on average in 2027, roughly twice as large if rates stay at current levels.

GS estimates higher rates slow consumer spending growth by about 0.2pp in 2027, mainly through weaker credit-financed durable goods demand (motor vehicles, recreation goods). Higher net interest income, since households are net lenders in aggregate, partly offsets it.

Higher funding costs drag business investment because firms spend more of revenue on interest when refinancing. Small businesses are more exposed, with about half their debt variable-rate. GS expects a drag of about 0.3pp on 2027 capex growth. Overall GDP growth is about 0.2pp lower in 2027, with a drag more than twice as large if market rates stay at current levels.

Two additional risks if rates persist: GS strategists expect equities to rise slightly over 10% by end-2027, but stable rates could limit upside, and flat equities through 2027 would cut consumer spending growth by just under 0.5pp. Higher rates have also revived fiscal sustainability concerns, because higher interest expense pushes the debt-to-GDP ratio up faster.

Kaplan's market direction call: the primary trend remains higher and the tactical setup is net positive, on four reasons: strong nominal GDP growth, superb earnings growth, supportive flow of funds, and a continuing investment super cycle. He expects Q4 to stay choppy but S&P to finish the year above today's level.

Kaplan calls higher rates a headwind, not a wrecking ball. The S&P P/E has fallen from 23x to 19x over the past year, and rate-sensitive groups show the impact (small cap, homebuilders, utilities, REITs, biotech, non-profitable tech). The spread of rates over the S&P earnings yield has been steady, and sustaining double-digit EPS growth with a healthy credit market is the key to absorbing more rate pressure.

Kaplan compares this to the 2022 tightening, when the Fed went over 500bps and stocks fell sharply. He believes the market already prices the rate strip (one more hike this year, about two more next year) and expects stocks to tolerate that, helped by a $2tr budget deficit and $1tr of AI capex.

The forward P/E of the median AI infrastructure stock fell from 32x in April to 22x six months later while the companies are delivering. Kaplan expects more air pockets and volatility, but US mega cap tech remains 'both the sword and the shield'.

VIX is within a point of YTD lows. Kaplan argues low index vol reflects high dispersion and low correlation, not an absence of tension, and says the cost of convexity is not prohibitive for left or right tail hedging.
Breadth has been very bad, but narrowness has been a constant of this bull market for four years. S&P 19x forward P/E is in the 76th percentile since 1990 but equals the ten-year average.

GS Weekly Execution Insights: after the SEC's proposed rescission of Reg NMS Rule 611 (Order Protection Rule), on-exchange continuous-session activity outside the NBBO is about 3.8% of share volume YTD (4.2% in May, 3.2% in March), likely from intermarket sweep orders and erroneous trade throughs. Over 64% of shares trade at the NBB or NBO, about 21% at the exact midpoint, about 32% including prints between the NBB/NBO and midpoint.

Flows: GS floor activity was a 4 out of 10. Long-only funds were slight net sellers driven by macro products, hedge funds slight net buyers driven by tech. GS sees no real signs of chasing. US L/S net leverage is at its lowest since April 2025 and near five-year lows (2nd percentile), so a continued index move higher would force investors to buy.
Chart of the day: European equities showed larger sensitivity to credit, but there were fewer spillovers to US equities (1-month correlation).

Calendar: US trade balance 8:30 AM, crude inventories, Eurozone retail sales, $58bn 3-year auction at 1 PM. Fed speakers: Williams, Bowman, Logan (voters), Musalem, Schmid (non-voters). Investor days: MRVL, ZS, NOMD, RZLV. Amazon Prime Day through 10/7. Earnings: RPM, LW pre-market, STZ post-market.

tension_points.bull_case: Kaplan says rates are a headwind, not a wrecking ball. Earnings are a bulwark, the rate-to-earnings-yield spread has been steady, the market already prices one more hike this year and about two next year, and a $2tr deficit plus $1tr of AI capex help stocks tolerate it.
tension_points.bear_case: The GS Economics Analyst sees drags on housing, consumer spending and capex, and warns stable rates could limit equity upside. Kaplan cites the 2022 tightening cycle, when stocks fell sharply.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Kaplan names sustaining double-digit EPS growth with a healthy credit market as the key. A failure of either would undermine the view.
